content:
I am looking for sources on formatting/best practices guidelines for including Lean code in formal papers. I specifically want to submit to DCDS but cannot find any reference to Lean in their guidelines at https://www.aimsciences.org/index/GuideforAuthors. I have a fully compiled project that supports my written submission.

Can anybody help me here?

Thank you in advance,
Ian
You can have a look at beautiful lean related papers on the arxiv, that come with their tex sources, and draw inspiration.

Thank you, Filippo! I've also learned (hopefully correctly) that just formatting the code according to mathlib standards is a big first step for this.

edit: i found the tex source for Buzzard's work. Exactly what I needed, thank you!
For older work people might be using the listings package but nowadays I recommend minted to everyone. Using a tex source for old work of mine might lead you to listings.
Afaik springer lncs doesn’t support minted because they insist on compiling their camera ready version with pdflatex.
This automatically implies that many logic related conferences in CS don’t support minted.

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

https://leanprover-community.github.io/papers.html
Contains a quite rich list.

This looks quite out of date, I think there were a lot more formalization papers published in 2025 than the four AFM articles! Everyone should contribute their papers to the bibliography.
website#701 was a PR to add all Lean-related ITP '25 papers. A pull request against that branch, fixing the missing ends, is welcome!
